def peek(seq):
    """ Retrieve the next element of a sequence

    Returns the first element and an iterable equivalent to the original
    sequence, still having the element retrieved.

    >>> seq = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
    >>> first, seq = peek(seq)
    >>> first
    0
    >>> list(seq)
    [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
    """
    iterator = iter(seq)
    item = next(iterator)
    return item, itertools.chain([item], iterator)


def peekn(n, seq):
    """Retrieve the first n elements of a sequence

    Returns a tuple of the first n elements and an iterable equivalent to the
    original sequence, still having those elements.

    >>> seq = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
    >>> first_two, seq = peekn(2, seq)
    >>> first_two
    (0, 1)
    >>> list(seq)
    [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]

    If there are fewer than n elements in the sequence, returns all of them.

    >>> seq = [0, 1]
    >>> first_two, seq = peekn(5, seq)
    >>> first_two
    (0, 1)
    >>> list(seq)
    [0, 1]
    """
    iterator = iter(seq)
    items = []
    for _ in range(n):
        try:
            item = next(iterator)
            items.append(item)
        except StopIteration:
            break
    return tuple(items), itertools.chain(items, iterator)
